We need to fix compilation errors. The test code uses JUnit 5 (jupiter) and Mockito, but those dependencies may not be present in environment. Probably we need to simplify the test to use JUnit 4? However the instruction: "You are an experienced Java developer tasked with fixing a piece of code that contains compilation errors." We need to modify the code to compile with available libraries. In this environment, likely only JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test) and maybe no Mockito. The imports include both JUnit5 and JUnit4, duplicates. We can replace with JUnit4 assertions and annotations.

Simplify: remove JUnit5 annotations like @Nested, @DisplayName, @BeforeAll, @AfterAll, @BeforeEach, @Test from JUnit5; use JUnit4 equivalents: @BeforeClass, @AfterClass, @Before, @Test (org.junit.Test). JUnit4 does not have @Nested. We'll flatten nested classes into separate test methods or keep inner static classes with @RunWith? Simpler: remove nested classes and just have test methods directly. But we can keep inner classes annotated with @RunWith? Not needed. To compile, we can keep them but remove JUnit5-specific annotations.

Also remove Mockito usage; we can replace mocked indicator with a simple stub implementation of Indicator returning constant 5. So we don't need Mockito.

Also ConstantIndicator generic inference issue: need to specify type: new ConstantIndicator<Num>(DecimalNum.valueOf(2)). Actually ConstantIndicator likely generic <Num>. So we can use new ConstantIndicator<>(DecimalNum.valueOf(2)); but compilation error earlier due to missing import? The ConstantIndicator class is likely in org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.ConstantIndicator. It expects Num type. The diamond should work. Maybe the error was because ConstantIndicator is generic but we didn't import. It is imported via org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.*; So fine. The inference error might be due to missing type parameter for NumericIndicator.of expecting Indicator<Num>. Should be okay.

But many errors stem from missing JUnit5 and Mockito packages. So rewrite imports to only JUnit4 and remove Mockito imports.

Also remove usage of atLeastOnce() and verify etc.

Implement a simple stub for mockIndicator: class ConstantIndicatorMock implements Indicator<Num> returning constant value.

Also remove usage of Mockito.anyInt().

Also remove @ExtendWith annotation.

Also remove duplicate imports.

Now adjust methods: replace assertThrows with try-catch and fail, or use JUnit4's ExpectedException rule? Simpler: use try { left.multipliedBy(null); fail(); } catch (NullPointerException e) {}.

Similarly for other assertThrows.

Also replace @BeforeAll static method with @BeforeClass static.

@BeforeEach with @Before.

@AfterAll with @AfterClass.

@DisplayName can be removed.

@Nested classes: we can keep inner static classes but without @Nested; JUnit4 will treat them as separate test classes? Not automatically. Simpler: flatten tests: move their methods into outer class. But we can keep inner classes annotated with @RunWith? Not needed. For compilation, inner classes can exist without annotations; the test methods inside will be recognized only if they are annotated with @Test and the class is public static? JUnit4 only runs top-level test classes, not inner ones unless they are static and annotated with @RunWith? Not needed for compilation. So we can keep them but they will not be executed, but compile.

Thus we just need to remove JUnit5 annotations to avoid missing imports.

Also remove imports of org.junit.jupiter.params.* etc.

Now adjust code accordingly.
